rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments on common pricing algorithms (AB 325 / SB 763)
rules.requirement: Businesses, including landlords, may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (two or more users, uses competitor data) as part of an agreement to restrain trade, and may not coerce users to adopt the algorithm's price recommendations. Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
rules.effective_date_note: Document states AB 325 and SB 763 took effect January 1, 2026.
rules.key_value: ban on using/distributing common pricing algorithms in price-fixing agreements or coercing adoption; civil fines up to $1 million; criminal fines up to $6 million for corporations
rules.penalty: Civil fines up to $1 million (AG or district attorney actions); criminal fines up to greater of $6 million or twice gain/loss for corporations and $1 million for individuals; treble damages and injunctive relief in private suits.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any business using or distributing common pricing algorithms, not limited to housing.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

parsed.doc_summary: Cleary Gottlieb alert (Jan 2026) on California's AB 325/SB 763 Cartwright Act amendments, effective 2026-01-01, banning common pricing algorithm use in price-fixing or coercion, with new civil and criminal penalties. Only the California state algorithmic pricing rule is in scope.
